Guayaquil: a bridge lit in blue at night
Guayaquil to the Galápagos Islands and Santa Cruz

After breakfast, transfer to the airport for the flight to the Galápagos Islands.

The flight is paid for separately.

On arrival at Baltra Airport, your guide will meet the group and help with the luggage.

The bus ride to the Itabaca Channel takes about 10 minutes.

The crossing to Santa Cruz takes around 5 minutes by motorboat.

Then drive across the island to Puerto Ayora.

The drive takes approximately 45 minutes.

Along the way, the landscape changes from red, rocky terrain in the north to greener highlands and the south of the island.

The group heads into the Santa Cruz highlands.

As you pass through farmland, you may see a range of plants and animals, including the finches associated with Darwin’s research.

The main aim is to see Galápagos giant tortoises in their natural habitat.

You may see tortoises of different ages and sizes.

Your guide explains how private farms help protect the tortoises and their habitat.

The next stop is the lava tunnels.

The tunnels formed as lava flows cooled unevenly.

Erosion has destroyed some tunnels, but others are well preserved.

Some lava tunnels reach up to 1 km in length.

Parts of the route may be difficult to navigate or contain fallen boulders.

Lunch in the highlands is included.

After the tour, transfer to Puerto Ayora.

Stay at the 3-star Fiesta hotel.

After check-in, you have free time to walk along the waterfront and explore the restaurants and souvenir shops.

Breakfast and lunch are included.
Volcanic hills and turquoise bays in the Galápagos Islands, Ecuador
